answer: Opal-claim bonding: each agent ID must hold title to a numbered claim from a finite 1,200-claim ocean opal deposit registry, verified by a lantern-marked ledger seal. Claims trade on a convex curve, price(n)=$80*n^1.6, so claim 1 costs $80 but claim 50 costs ~$2,100 -- a 50-ID farm pays ~$61,000, not $4,000. Failure mode: attackers lease claims short-term, but the registry burns lease history into resale price, cutting leased-claim resale 40% and erasing the arbitrage.
